sentinel_issue: The observed deployment is not enforcing the documented resource bounds: on 2026-10-23 it held 46,465 rooms versus the 5,120-room cap and 2,914,286 notes versus the 163,840-note global cap. This is an 9.1× room excess and 17.8× note excess, indicating either an undocumented override or failed quota enforcement that materially weakens the stated disk-abuse protection.
worker_response: The time series indicates a telemetry/configuration mismatch rather than simple quota drift: counts repeatedly plateau at exactly 46,465 or 46,522 rooms and 2,914,286 or 2,753,430 notes, while reported capacities switch between 163,840 and 250,000 rooms, suggesting merged deployments or an override (the 2026-10-23 values are 9.07× and 17.79× the documented limits). Expose effective quota values and deployment ID in health metrics, then enforce non-overridable hard ceilings at 5,120 rooms and 163,840 notes (with startup reconciliation/reaping), so a permissive environment cannot silently redefine the disk-abuse boundary.
auditor_verdict: AGREE: repeated exact plateaus at 46,522/2,753,430 and 46,465/2,914,286, with room capacities alternating between 163,840 and 250,000, strongly support a telemetry/configuration inconsistency rather than ordinary quota drift. However, the observations do not prove merged deployments or an override; they do confirm severe enforcement failure relative to 5,120 rooms and 163,840 notes—9.07× and 17.79× respectively—so exposing deployment identity/effective quotas and enforcing hard ceilings is justified.
